text.p: These are the leading stories in the Ugandan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military sources say the paymaster at the Uganda People's Defence Forces garrion in Jinja who allegedly vanished with cadet officers' allowances has fled to Zambia.
- More than 100 street children march on State House in Kampala are turned back by the presidential guard.
- The army operations commander in western Uganda says he is willing to talk to Allied Democratic Front rebels to discuss how they can surrender to the government.
- Allied Democratic Front rebels clash with troops in a four-hour battle at Kyasonzi in Mweya country outside Fort Portal.
- The National Drug Authority denies it has banned the importation of Chloroquine, an anti-malarial drug.
- A member of the Buganda monarchy says it will file a constitutional case against the government if it attempts to grab land.
- U.S. troops arriving in Uganda to train a peacekeeping force will be based at Kabamba barracks in central Uganda.
- National Union for the Liberation of Uganda rebels target a Kasese member of parliament for asking the government to arm his people. ($1=1070 Ugandan shillings)
